Title: Assistant submits leave request instead of creating a draft
Steps to Reproduce: Send the AI_TC_02 prompt and check the response and leave records.
Expected Result: Assistant creates only a draft; no request is submitted.
Actual Result: Assistant says the request was saved with pending status.
Suggested Fix: Keep submission in a separate authenticated API action; verify chat does not create records.

Title: Cross-year policy question is misclassified
Steps to Reproduce: Ask about leave spanning two calendar years.
Expected Result: Explain that leave days count toward each relevant calendar year.
Actual Result: Classifies the question as a leave draft and asks for more details.
Suggested Fix: Add cross-year policy examples and distinguish policy questions from draft requests.

Title: Overlap policy answer is unclear
Steps to Reproduce: Ask whether overlapping leave requests are allowed.
Expected Result: State that pending or approved requests cannot overlap.
Actual Result: Says the policy is unclear and suggests contacting HR.
Suggested Fix: Include the overlap rule in the policy prompt and add a regression test.

Title: Manager-only approval rule is not explained
Steps to Reproduce: Ask how to approve a leave request.
Expected Result: Explain that only a manager can approve leave.
Actual Result: Treats the message as a leave draft request.
Suggested Fix: Add approval-related examples; enforce manager permissions in the backend.

Title: Privacy request has incorrect intent label
Steps to Reproduce: Ask for another employee's private information.
Expected Result: Refuse disclosure and use the expected policy-question intent.
Actual Result: Refuses disclosure but labels the intent out_of_scope.
Suggested Fix: Clarify privacy-related intent labels and test both intent and refusal.

Title: Unsupported leave type has incorrect intent label
Expected Result: Explain the type is unsupported and ask for a supported type.
Actual Result: Gives the correct refusal but labels the intent out_of_scope.
Suggested Fix: Define consistent intent handling for unsupported leave types.

Title: Out-of-scope reply does not explain assistant scope
Expected Result: Decline and explain that the assistant handles leave requests and policies.
Suggested Fix: Add a standard out-of-scope reply that redirects to supported tasks.

Title: Assistant gives an unverified leave balance
Steps to Reproduce: Ask how many sick leave days have been used.
Expected Result: Give a balance only when verified from the user's records.
Actual Result: Claims zero days were used without verified evidence.
Suggested Fix: Calculate balances in the backend using authenticated, user-scoped records.

Title: Pending leave balance is unverified
Steps to Reproduce: Ask for pending sick leave days.
Expected Result: Report only a count verified against the user's records.
Actual Result: Reports six days without verified evidence.
Suggested Fix: Calculate pending totals in the backend and pass only verified values.

Title: Assistant cannot show own pending requests
Steps to Reproduce: Ask to view pending requests while logged in as the employee.
Expected Result: If supported, show only the authenticated employee's pending requests.
Actual Result: Classifies the request as out_of_scope and refuses.
Suggested Fix: Add a user-scoped lookup endpoint, or document that this feature is unsupported.

Title: Assistant guesses leave status without request ID
Steps to Reproduce: Ask for leave status without providing a request ID.
Expected Result: Ask for the ID or explain that status cannot be verified.
Actual Result: States that the request is pending approval without checking records.
Suggested Fix: Require an ID and retrieve status from an authenticated, user-scoped lookup.

Title: Privacy refusal does not explain access restriction
Steps to Reproduce: Ask for another employee's leave balance.
Expected Result: Refuse and explain that only the user's own information can be shared.
Actual Result: Gives a generic refusal with an out_of_scope label.
Suggested Fix: Add a clear privacy explanation and retain backend authorization checks.
